Vendor Stability.content: Whistic was founded in **2015** and has been operating for approximately **11 years** (as of 2026). The company is headquartered in Pleasant Grove, Utah.**Funding:** Whistic has raised a total of **$51.1M** across 5 funding rounds. Key rounds include:- **Seed Round:** $115K on March 1, 2016- **Series A:** $12M on July 20, 2020, led by Emergence Capital- **Series B:** $35M on June 7, 2022, led by JMI Equity, with participation from Forgepoint Capital and existing investors Emergence Capital, Album VC, and FJ Labs**Team Size:** Employee estimates vary. PitchBook reports **76 employees** as of 2024. Other sources estimate 48 employees (as of June 2026), 80 employees (as of May 2024), or 51-200.**Leadership Departures:** Nick Sorensen served as CEO from 2017 until approximately August 2025. Juan Rodriguez is now listed as CEO and Founder as of August 2025.**Layoffs & Acquisition Rumors:** No known layoffs have been publicly reported. There is no evidence of Whistic being acquired. However, one third-party analysis notes that with ~$51M total raised and no later round since 2022, the company has a "smaller war chest than category neighbors, so acquisition risk". A Glassdoor review from October 2024 expressed concern that the company is "struggling and will layoff at any time," but this is an isolated, anonymous opinion, not confirmed by any public reporting.**Financial Distress:** No public signs of financial distress have been reported.

Incident History.content: **Data Breaches (Whistic itself):** No public records of Whistic suffering a data breach were found. Whistic's own platform includes a "Vendor Monitoring" feature that detects publicly available breach records associated with third-party vendors and embeds them into assessment contexts. This is a feature Whistic sells to customers, not an indication of a Whistic breach.**Outages or Service Failures:** No major outages or service failures were found in public records.**Public Security Incidents:** No public security incidents involving Whistic were found in news reports or researcher disclosures.**Lawsuits:** No lawsuits related to data handling or security involving Whistic were found.
Incident History.source_type: self-reported (search found no incidents; explicitly disclosed as a search result, not a guarantee)

Community Signal.content: **Overall Sentiment:** User sentiment is generally positive, with an average rating of **4.6 out of 5 stars on G2** and **4.0 out of 5 stars** on alternative.me.**Common Praise:**- **Intuitive and easy to use**- **Streamlines workflows and saves time** on vendor security assessments- **Reduces questionnaire time** from weeks to days or minutes- **Top-tier support** for launching VRM programs**Common Complaints:**- **Limited customization and reporting options**- **Difficulty with mass data export** for external reporting tools- **Reporting constraints** become more limiting with larger VRM programs- One 2021 review called the product "terrible" and "overpriced"**Recurring Patterns:** The most frequently cited frustration is limited reporting capabilities and export options, which may be a dealbreaker for larger organizations with complex reporting needs.**Users Leaving:** No clear evidence that users are leaving for competitors. Competitors mentioned as alternatives include Bitsight, BlueVoyant, and LogicGate.

Data Handling Posture.content: **Data Collected:** Whistic collects personal data including first and last name, email address, and other information provided during service use. The platform also stores customer Content and Customer Data such as security controls, audits, certifications, questionnaires, answers, and other documents uploaded or stored through the Services.**Data Hosting:** Whistic is built on the **AWS Bedrock** framework. Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2) and at rest (AES-256). Specific hosting regions are not detailed in public documentation.**Data Retention:** Whistic states: "We do not store data beyond processing requirements". A detailed retention policy was not found in public materials.**AI Model Training:** Whistic explicitly states: **"No data used for AI model training"** and **"We don't share your data with external parties"**. The company says it does not use customer data to train AI models.**Subprocessors:** Whistic's public privacy policy does not appear to list specific subprocessors. The company notes that "every external company we work with has a contract... which clearly sets out our expectations and requirements in handling personal information", but a full subprocessor list was not found in public documentation. The platform relies on **AWS Bedrock** as an underlying infrastructure provider.**Vagueness:** The privacy policy notes that it "does not cover Personal Data that we process as a service provider or processor to provide services to our customers", creating some ambiguity about how customer data is handled in different contexts.

Integration Risk.content: **Integration Methods:**- **Public API** (GraphQL) providing programmatic access to vendor data, document uploads, report generation, and automation- **Reporting API** available at `https://graphql.whistic.com` requiring an API key- **Webhook** integrations- **BETA MCP (Model Context Protocol)** server for AI assistant integration- **No-code** built-in reporting features for simple exports**Data Export & Switching:** - Data can be pulled via API (contact CSM)- Reports can be exported as Excel files- **Critical limitation:** The API is "designed for dynamic scripts and automation rather than simple data exports" and "responses require programming knowledge to aggregate and process effectively"- Users have reported **difficulty with mass data export** for external reporting tools- No documented data portability or bulk export feature was found**Dependencies:**- Built on **AWS Bedrock** for AI capabilities- Relies on AWS infrastructure for hosting and security**Breaking Changes:** No known integration failures or breaking changes reported by users were found.**Lock-in Risk:** Medium. While the platform offers API access, the lack of simple mass export capabilities and reported difficulty with bulk data extraction suggest switching away could be costly and time-consuming, especially for organizations with extensive vendor assessment data stored in the platform.
